#1853. Angry Manchester United fans react to Michael Carrick sacking as new statement sent

The Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) have hit out at the club’s owners after Michael Carrick’s sacking marked another “depressing moment” at Old Trafford.

Carrick was relieved of his duties on Thursday morning, with United sitting 18th in the Premier League table after one win from their opening 10 matches.

It is expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as his replacement, though the timing of that has been complicated slightly by it being an international break and the USA preparing for two important Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti.

Confirmation of Carrick’s sacking came after United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco on Wednesday to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

The MUST paid tribute to Carrick, who won five Premier League titles with United as a player, as the group instead took aim at Ratcliffe and the club’s majority owners, the Glazers.

“Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United,” an MUST statement read.

“We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.

“The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.

“They lie with the ownership. The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.”

The United fans had continued to stick with Carrick, even as results collapsed in recent weeks.

After the 3-0 defeat at home by Bournemouth last month, the Stretford End sung Carrick’s name as he made his way off the pitch.

How Man Utd could line up in Pochettino’s first game against Liverpool

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

As soon as he entered the tunnel, the mood shifted and there were loud boos for the players in front of that stand.

It has added to the unhappy feeling at United, in the stands and in the dressing room. Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised Wilcox and the club’s summer recruitment after United were beaten by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, before Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics in another explosive interview after the thrashing by Como.

“The earlier Stretford End banner declaring, ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace’ was a warning,” the MUST continued in their criticism of ownership.

“The unprecedented scale of the booing at Old Trafford, alongside public criticism from senior players in recent weeks, now points to a deeper deterioration.

“These are signs of a club becoming more divided, with the bond between supporters, players and those running Manchester United under increasing strain.”

No senior figures at United put their name to the official statement confirming Carrick’s sacking.

The MUST urged United executives to put greater emphasis on accountability to help improve the relationship between fans and those running the club.

“The owners must allow senior club management to change direction: show accountability, rebuild trust, listen to supporters and recognise that their loyalty is fundamental to football success,” the group said.

“Another change of head coach cannot repair what the ownership continues to undermine.”

#1852. Tottenham transfer news: Spurs 'join' Arsenal in race for £40m talisman scoring every 85 minutes

By Lewis Blain | 12 Nov 2026 07:38

Tottenham Hotspur have joined arch-rivals Arsenal in the race to sign AC Monza striker Gustavo Varela ahead of the January transfer window.

The 21-year-old has enjoyed a remarkable rise over the past year, becoming one of Serie A's most prolific forwards despite playing for a struggling side.

However, Spurs and their rivals could face a battle to convince Monza to part with their prized asset midway through the season.

According to reports in Portugal (via Sport Witness), Tottenham, Juventus and Inter Milan have all joined the growing list of clubs monitoring Varela.

Arsenal were already keeping tabs on the striker, alongside Napoli and LaLiga giants Barcelona, meaning competition for his signature is increasing.

Spurs have not submitted an offer or opened formal negotiations, with their interest currently at the monitoring stage.

Monza are reluctant to sell in January, viewing Varela as essential to their fight against relegation. It is believed that the Italian side could demand up to €50m (£42m).

Varela's rise has been particularly impressive.

Having struggled for regular opportunities during a loan spell at Gil Vicente, he eventually established himself in the first team last January, finishing the campaign with seven goals and three assists in 33 appearances.

His move to Monza during the summer has taken his career to another level, with the forward scoring 11 goals in 11 games this season, finding the net once every 85 minutes despite the club sitting 18th in Serie A on just seven points. He has also earned his first senior Portugal call-up under Jorge Jesus.

Those numbers make it easy to understand why so many clubs are taking notice.

Varela has even attracted comparisons with former Chelsea and Wolves striker Diego Costa, adding another intriguing dimension to his growing reputation.

For Tottenham, the appeal is obvious, as the Portuguese talisman could offer a much-needed attacking option, while Arsenal and Barceona's interest suggests his performances are attracting attention well beyond Italy.

However, spending upwards of £42m on a striker with only a short period of senior-level consistency would represent a considerable investment.

His extraordinary scoring rate makes him an exciting prospect, but Monza's reluctance to sell means January could prove a difficult time to secure his signature.

#1848. Zinedine Zidane defends Chelsea star after ‘nightmare’ performance in France defeat

Zinedine Zidane has defended Malo Gusto following the Chelsea defender’s poor performance during France’s 3-1 defeat to Italy on Thursday night.

Michael Olise gave France an early lead in Milan but a double from Pio Esposito, plus a goal from Davide Frattesi, handed Zidane his first loss since taking over from Didier Deschamps in July.

Gusto, who has started just three Premier League games for Chelsea this season, was selected at right-back but struggled against Nicolo Cambiaghi and gave away the foul which led to Italy’s penalty in the second half.

French media described Gusto’s performance as a ‘nightmare’, while RMC Sport host Daniel Riolo tore into the Chelsea defender after France’s defeat.

‘Malo Gusto, who never plays for his club, I don’t even know what he’s doing there,’ Riolo said. ‘He was toyed with by Bologna’s winger… I don’t understand why Zaire-Emery isn’t playing. We don’t have any full-backs, so you play with the wingers tucked in.’

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

When asked about Gusto’s performance after France’s defeat, Zidane replied: ‘He was called up, he played his part, he conceded the penalty, these things happen.

‘I don’t think we can say that he had a bad game.

‘So there you have it, now I’m doing the analysis as a whole anyway, I’m not talking about individuals.’

France, who sit second in their Nations League Group A behind Italy, will now play Turkey in their final group game on Sunday night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

But despite the scoreline against Italy, Zidane has urged his players not to panic.

‘There were some good things, especially in the first half where we should have focused on what we did well. After that, we did some less good things,’ Zidane told TF1.

‘We lost the match, so naturally there were some more complicated situations, particularly in duels and one-on-one situations, we weren’t quite as good. It’s all part of the learning process.

‘When we were in difficulty, we didn’t know how to react and stay within the game plan we had put in place. We did it in the first half, but when they took the lead, we became a little scattered, especially defensively.

‘Tonight wasn’t a bad game. There’s room for improvement. I told the players we shouldn’t panic. We became more fragile as the match went on. What I told them is that it was a defeat, but not entirely deserved.

‘We did some good things and some not-so-good things. We’ll analyse it when we’re in Bordeaux to prepare for our match. We just need to rest and focus on the game we have left.’

#1845. Harry Kane becomes England’s most-capped men’s player with 126th appearance

Harry Kane has broken the all-time record for the most appearances by an England men’s player.

By leading his country out against Croatia on Thursday evening, alongside his four children, the England captain overtook Peter Shilton’s long-standing record to move top of the all-time caps list with his 126th appearance.

Shilton was involved in a commemorative tribute to Kane before kick-off in the Nations League game at Wembley, before Prince William presented him with a signed ‘126’ shirt.

The 33-year-old’s tribute before the match also included him parading his Ballon d’Or trophy in front of the Wembley crowd. It is the first time the award for best player has been on English soil since Kane was crowned its winner at the London Palladium 17 days ago.

Kane is already the top scorer in the history of the national team, having netted 91 goals in 125 caps before taking the field against Croatia on Thursday evening.

The skipper has said he wants to “set a challenge” for future England players to beat his caps record.

Midfielders Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice boast 60 and 80 caps at the ages of 23 and 27, respectively, and Kane said on Wednesday: “Look at how young they are, I will try and give them a good number to catch.”

Billy Wright and Bobby Moore shared the record for the most England caps as captain for decades, having each led the Three Lions out 90 times. But having overtaken that record earlier this year, Kane is now on cap 98 as skipper, and is expected to reach a century next year.

The final of four matches during the last international break saw England defeat Czechia 3-0 with two goals from Kane and the other, an own goal, having been set up by the captain.

After the match, Bellingham said of Kane: “He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him.” England head coach Thomas Tuchel recently admitted he had “run out of superlatives” with which to describe Kane.

#1843. Chelsea transfer news: Barcelona eye £75m-rated Blues star as Xabi Alonso sale stance now revealed

By Lewis Blain | 12 Nov 2026 08:01

Chelsea are preparing for further interest in Levi Colwill, with Barcelona among the clubs monitoring the England international.

The 23-year-old has established himself as a key figure under Xabi Alonso, making him an attractive proposition for several European heavyweights.

However, the Blues are determined to retain their homegrown defender and are already considering fresh contract talks to strengthen their position.

According to reports, Chelsea expect interest in Colwill to increase over the coming months, with Barcelona already among his admirers.

The Spanish giants are understood to be monitoring the situation, although there are doubts over whether they could afford a deal given their ongoing financial difficulties.

Colwill's profile makes him an increasingly sought-after defender, particularly as a young, left-footed centre-back with considerable potential.

Chelsea, though, are adamant that he is not for sale under any circumstances, with Alonso viewing the £75m-rated defender as a central part of his plans at Stamford Bridge.

The England international has started all but one Premier League match this season and has provided some much-needed stability in a position that has caused problems for the club in recent campaigns.

It is also believed that Chelsea are preparing fresh discussions over an improved contract, despite Colwill already being tied down until the summer of 2029.

Chelsea would be foolish to entertain the prospect of selling Colwill, particularly given the difficulty of finding an established left-sided centre-back of his age and ability.

At just 23, he has already demonstrated his value in the Premier League and offers Alonso an important combination of technical quality, composure and defensive versatility.

His status as a Cobham academy graduate also makes him an important figure for the club, while losing him would create another significant problem in an area that has lacked consistency.

Barcelona's interest is understandable, but Chelsea have little incentive to negotiate, especially when Colwill remains under contract for another three years.

An improved deal would be a sensible move, although the priority should be ensuring he remains a cornerstone of Alonso's defensive plans for the foreseeable future.

#1842. Declan Rice reveals he's stepped back from social media because it can 'ruin your whole day' after sick trolling of him and his girlfriend - as he poses in new photoshoot

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:36 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 08:45 EST, 9 November 2026

Declan Rice has opened up about reducing his use of social media - citing the mental toll it can have.

The Arsenal and England midfielder has been subjected to online abuse in the past - with his long-term partner Lauren Fryer having also been targeted.

Online abuse about her appearance had led to Fryer wiping all posts from her Instagram page back in 2024.

While Rice still has an Instagram account, he quit X three years ago as a result of the negativity that app can bring.

'I've not been back on the app since,' he told GQ Magazine - after being named among their Men of the Year. 'You could be having a great morning. You read one thing, and it just ruins your whole day.

'I feel like that's one of my strongest points... the ability to block out noise and not deal with that kind of stuff.'

Declan Rice has revealed he quit X three years ago due to the abuse he would receive online

Rice and long-term partner Lauren Fryer have been targeted in the past (pair pictured with their son Jude in May)

The midfielder says one post could 'ruin' his whole day - even if he was a great day beforehand

Rice, who has a four-year-old son called Jude with Fryer, is worried about the impact of social media on the younger generations.

'Screen time, for me, isn't a big thing,' he says of his own personal phone usage. 'I think social media for kids is 100 per cent a problem. I don't feel like there's as much personality now as there was a few years ago.'

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport last month, the 27-year-old is closing in on a new long-term deal at Arsenal believed to be worth around £350,000 per week.

The contract will put him on a level footing with Bukayo Saka at the top of the club's salary list.

And speaking about money in football as a whole, Rice told GQ Magazine that the finances within the sport are 'ridiculous' and despite his wealth he still wants to set a good example to his son Jude.

'The money that's in football as a whole is just ridiculous,' he continued. 'It's important to understand what things cost, even if you don't have to worry about paying for them.

'You still want to teach your kid values, not wanting them to be spoiled. You want them to work and to understand the value of life and money.

'It makes you more comfortable to be able to do things. But I don't wake up and think, "Oh, I've got loads of money", it's not the end goal.'

The 27-year-old is worried about the pitfalls of social media on the younger generations

Rice's focus will now be on his country with England hosting Croatia on Thursday night in the UEFA Nations League before travelling to World Cup champions Spain on Sunday.

Going into the November international break, the midfielder is enjoying a fine season with Arsenal who sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League with 27 points from their opening 10 matches.

#1841. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

#1839. Michael Carrick issues first statement after Manchester United sacking

Michael Carrick has thanked Manchester United’s players and supporters following his sacking and insists he wants ‘nothing but success’ for the club.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino was officially announced as his replacement on Friday afternoon.

The 45-year-old returned to United in January following Ruben Amorim’s departure and joined on an interim deal until the end of last season.

Carrick was then rewarded with a two-year contract in May following United’s impressive end to the Premier League campaign, with no club in the top flight securing more points than the 36 United collected following Carrick’s arrival.

However, United have made a poor start to this season, registering just one win in 10 Premier League games – a run of results which has left the team 18th in the table.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Carrick retained the backing from United’s supporters, who have heavily booed the players during their dismal run of form, but the club’s hierarchy have opted to make a change by bringing in Pochettino.

In his statement which was released on Friday, Carrick wrote: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

‘It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.

‘I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

‘I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

#1838. Portugal vs. Denmark: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of UEFA Nations League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 08:51, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 08:51

Portugal and Denmark will lock horns in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday.

Denmark and Portugal have faced each other a total of 19 times on the international stage across all competitions, including friendlies.

Portugal comfortably lead the overall head-to-head record with 13 victories, while Denmark have only beaten A Selecao das Quinas on four occasions, and there have also been two draws played out between the two nations.

The very first meeting between Denmark and Portugal was a friendly that took place back in June 1966 when Jose Torres scored twice in a 3-1 victory for A Selecao das Quinas in Esbjerg.

Over a 34-year period, Portugal won seven and drew one of their first eight encounters with Denmark, including a thumping 5-0 home victory in Euro 1972 qualifying - their biggest win over the Danes to date.

Like London buses, two Danish victories then came at once, with a 4-2 friendly win on home soil in September 2006 followed two years later by a 3-2 away success in Lisbon in 2010 World Cup qualifying.

Portugal won only one of their five meetings with Denmark over a five-year period up until October 2011 when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat in Euro 2012 qualifying.

A Selecao das Quinas then posted three straight wins over Denmark, before the Danes claimed a slender 1-0 first-leg victory in the 2024-25 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals courtesy of a second-half strike from Rasmus Hojlund.

However, Portugal bounced back just three days later and prevailed 5-2 after extra time in the second leg in Lisbon, with Cristiano Ronaldo and Francisco Trincao (2) among the goalscorers in the thrilling contest.

The last meeting between the two teams came in the 2026-27 Nations League, with Portugal posting a 4-2 win over Denmark.

Saturday's match will be Portugal's first fixture since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement.

Oct 01, 2026: Denmark 2-4 Portugal (UEFA Nations League Group Stage)

Mar 23, 2025: Portugal 5-2 Denmark (a.e.t) (UEFA Nations League Quarter-Final Second Leg)

Mar 20, 2025: Denmark 1-0 Portugal (UEFA Nations League Quarter-Final First Leg)

Oct 08, 2015: Portugal 1-0 Denmark (European Championship Qualifiers)

Oct 14, 2014: Denmark 0-1 Portugal (European Championship Qualifiers)

Jun 13, 2012: Denmark 2-3 Portugal (European Championship Group Stage)

Oct 11, 2011: Denmark 2-1 Portugal (European Championship Group Stage)

Oct 08, 2010: Portugal 3-1 Denmark (European Championship Group Stage)

Sept 05, 2009: Denmark 1-1 Portugal (World Cup Qualifier)

Sept 10, 2008: Portugal 2-3 Denmark (World Cup Qualifier)

#1836. Mancini calls on Italy players to be more courageous

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto Mancini has called on his Italy players "to improve in our courage" despite their impressive victory over France on Thursday.

The Azzurri defeated Zinedine Zidane's side 3-1 in the Nations League, with a goal from Davide Frattesi and brace from Francesco Pio Esposito clinching a vital win in their campaign.

After failing to do so in the previous six meetings (D2, L4), Italy won a home match against France for the first time since a 2-1 victory in May 1962.

Sebastiano Esposito also missed a penalty in the victory, but it mattered little as Italy moved top of Group A1 ahead of a huge encounter with Belgium.

Just one point separates Italy and third-place Belgium ahead of their meeting on Sunday, with France level on points with the Azzurri ahead of hosting Turkiye.

Mancini took pride in Italy's resilience against France, but insisted his players must get used to such situations sooner rather than later.

"I gave what I could give, but the players were the ones who received it quickly, even if we know there is a long road ahead of us," said Mancini in his press conference.

"After going behind so early, we could've conceded another three or four if we'd let our heads drop, instead we did well to keep calm.

"We've got to improve in our courage; the young players must do things enough times that they become normal.

"It takes time, and I hope the older figures in the team can help the process."

"We hope he can score many more goals. Gigi Riva had 35 and it’s not so far away, so we hope he can get there," added Mancini.

"We need goals from Pio and everyone else, but he can certainly score many."

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

#1834. Japan vs Brazil - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 09:22

The Singapore National Stadium stages an international friendly fixture between Japan and Brazil on Saturday.

These two nations renew acquaintances just five months after locking horns in the last 32 of the 2026 World Cup, with the South American giants coming from behind to win 2-1 in Houston.

Just over a week after edging past Japan in June, Brazil’s World Cup journey was ended by Norway (2-1) at the last-16 stage, and they have since taken part in three friendly matches between September and October, scoring nine goals in the process.

An experimental Selecao outfit were held to a 1-1 draw by Australia, though a stronger, fired-up side responded by securing a 4-2 comeback victory over the Socceroos in a heated encounter just four days later.

Carlo Ancelotti then celebrated his 12th victory in 20 matches as Brazil head coach with a comfortable 4-0 success against India, courtesy of first-half strikes from Estevao Willian and Pedro, before Samuel Lino netted a second-half brace.

Brazil will conclude 2026 with two more friendlies against Japan and Singapore this month, facing the latter next Tuesday, before Ancelotti turns his attention to 2027's warm-up friendlies and the start of 2030 World Cup qualifying, all while building a fresh generation of talent ahead of the 2028 Copa America.

Ranked sixth in the world by FIFA, Brazil boast an impressive head-to-head record over Saturday’s opponents Japan, winning 12 of their 15 meetings in all competitions (D2 L1). The Selecao have also scored at least twice on 12 of those occasions.

Since their round-of-32 elimination at the World Cup this summer, Japan have put together a four-game unbeaten run in friendly fixtures, including three triumphs over South American opposition.

The Samurai Blue secured back-to-back home victories against Uruguay and Venezuela in September, beating the former 3-1 and the latter 2-1, with Ayase Ueda scoring three goals off the substitutes’ bench across both matches.

Hajime Moriyasu’s men then prevailed 5-4 on penalties against Ecuador following a goalless stalemate at the start of October, before winning 2-1 against New Zealand in their most recent friendly fixture courtesy of goals from Ueda and Ritsu Doan.

Since September 2025, Japan have only been beaten in one of their last 15 international matches across all competitions (W10 D4), and that lone defeat was the aforementioned World Cup loss to Brazil in June when they conceded a 95th-minute goal.

However, this impressive run did include their first and only victory over the five-time world champions in October last year, when the Samurai Blue came from two goals down at half time to secure a memorable 3-2 friendly win – Ueda (again) scored what proved to be the winner.

Japan will follow up their latest battle with Brazil this weekend by rounding off 2026 against Paraguay next Tuesday, playing once again at the Singapore National Stadium just a few hours after the Selecao have faced the hosts.

Japan’s 28-man squad does not include star striker Ueda, winger Kaoru Mitoma or defender Takehiro Tomiyasu as they all remain sidelined with injuries.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki could continue between the sticks and captain Ko Itakura is likely to start at the heart of the defence, while Daichi Kamada, Ao Tanaka and Kaishu Sano could all link up in midfield.

Koki Ogawa has scored 11 goals in 18 international appearances for Japan and will hope to lead the line this weekend, while Takumi Minamino, Junya Ito, Takefusa Kubo and Daizen Maeda are also contenders to start in the final third.

As for Brazil, Ancelotti has named a youthful 26-man squad that does not include senior stars including Alisson Becker, Marquinhos, Matheus Cunha and Joao Pedro, the latter of whom remains sidelined through injury.

However, Raphinha has been included despite having recently recovered from a muscle injury. Barcelona boss Hansi Flick was left frustrated by the attacker’s “not ideal” selection, but it is understood that his minutes will be managed during the international break.

Raphinha could therefore begin as a substitute this weekend, with Real Madrid duo Endrick and Vinicius Junior linking up in attack alongside either Rayan or Estevao.

Arsenal pair Bruno Guimaraes and Gabriel Magalhaes are both contenders to play in midfield and defence respectively, while Allan, Alisson Santana, Marlon Gomes, Andre, Jonathan Jesus and Lucas Perri are six uncapped players who could make their Brazil debut.

Z. Suzuki; Seko, Itakura, Ito; Sugawara, Kamada, Tanaka, Nakamura; Kubo, Maeda; Ogawa

Bento; Wesley, Jair Cunha, Gabriel, Augusto; Bontempo, Gomes, Santos; Rayan, Endrick, Vinicius Jr

While neither Japan nor Brazil will be at full strength, there should still be plenty of talent on display in what promises to be an entertaining, end-to-end contest, given that at least three goals have been scored in eight of the last nine meetings between these two nations.

Out for revenge following their summer World Cup heartache against the Selecao, a determined Samurai Blue outfit have the credentials to frustrate Ancelotti's men and claim a share of the spoils in Singapore.

#1833. England 2-1 Croatia: Harry Kane with the winner to cap special night

England captain Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th cap with a 92nd international goal as the skipper’s spot-kick sealed a 2-1 win over Croatia and set up a Nations League shootout in Spain.

The irrepressible 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley, where the Bayern Munich sharpshooter’s Ballon d’Or triumph was celebrated along with his landmark appearance.

Kane became the most capped Englishman in history, having last month equalled the record held by Peter Shilton, who was on hand to make a pre-match presentation to the star along with the Prince of Wales.

The striker looked like he would be denied a customary goal on this special night as Croatia defended diligently before capitalising on a second-half error to cancel out Morgan Rogers’ opener.

Petar Sucic pounced on a poor Jarell Quansah header, but the England defender quickly won a penalty that Kane slammed home as the nation’s all-time scorer netted in a fifth successive game.

Thomas Tuchel’s men had already effectively secured qualification for March’s Nations League quarter-finals before this match, but Thursday’s victory rubberstamped it and kept hopes alive of winning Group A3 heading into Sunday’s trip to leaders Spain.

England failed to kick on after taking a 24th-minute lead and the crowd thinned, with half-time refreshments proving more appealing than the performance. The absence of added time spoke volumes.

Kane was stopped from scoring England’s second of the night six minutes into the second half as Josip Stanisic got in the way of a low Declan Rice ball.

Bellingham saw an attempt denied and Anthony Gordon tried his luck before England gifted Croatia a way back.

Josko Gvardiol was there to help bundle on a corner that Quansah attempted to nod back to Joran Pickford, only for Sucic to capitalise on the weak header and slam home in the 59th minute.

It was a costly defensive mistake, but the England centre-back soon benefitted from one at the other end after Ivan Smolcic wrestled him to the ground at a corner.

Referee Morten Krogh was sent to the monitor and awarded a penalty that Kane thumped home in the 64th minute.

Sucic was denied another leveller as Croatia looked to respond, with both sides making changes to alter the dynamics.

Ben White was among those introduced and booed by some of the England faithful. Croatia veteran Luka Modric received a far warmer reception.

Nikola Vlasic went close as the visitors pushed and Quansah blocked an Ante Budimir shot after James Garner was denied a first England goal by an offside in the build-up.

Budimir went close in stoppage time, but England held out as attention turns to Madrid.

#1831. Harry Kane makes sure it’s business as usual on his special night for England

As Manchester United again dominated the headlines with their latest managerial dice-roll, Harry Kane made sure he wouldn’t be overshadowed.

On a night that was all about England’s greatest goalscorer, on his record-breaking 126th cap, Kane made sure it remained all about Kane. And rightly so.

England’s No9 pulled the lever, scored the winner, and set up a tantalising showstopper on Sunday. Whoever wins between England and Spain this weekend will finish top of their Nations League group, and with it an easier quarter-final opponent in March.

Just 17 days after winning the Ballon d’Or, being crowned the finest footballer on the planet, Kane overtook Peter Shilton at Wembley to claim the all-time England appearance record for himself. Shilton, Kane’s family and Prince William were all on hand to celebrate with him.

And how better to mark the occasion, than with the winning goal. A penalty struck down the middle was typical of a 33-year-old in a hurry to hunt down further records, still relentlessly hard-working and keen to prove that the autumn of his career can show him to be even more influential for club and country.

He has the most goals in England’s history, this his 92nd, and now the most caps, too; the England records just continue to tumble for Kane. Most goals at major tournaments. Most goals in a calendar year. Most appearances as captain. Most games won. Most, most, most, most.

Yet for a long time this was a night that was going England’s way, but not Kane’s. And then when Petar Susic seized on a Jarell Quansah mistake to equalise, the celebrations were at risk of ending early.

#1830. Crisis-hit FIFA chief Gianni Infantino 'requested VIP treatment for his daughters and their dogs at Miami airport'

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 09:47 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:07 EST, 9 November 2026

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing more uncomfortable questions after it emerged that his office asked for 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their pet dogs on a trip from Miami to Qatar.

Infantino's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months, with honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announcing on Thursday that he will stand against Infantino in next year's presidential election.

On Thursday, The Times revealed that back in May, Infantino's presidential office wrote to Miami airport officials asking for someone to 'assist' three of his daughters - and their pets - through security for a personal trip to Qatar.

Miami airport's VIP protocol reportedly allows diplomats and other special guests to be escorted through security checkpoints up to the door of the plane. Officers can also request early boarding.

These privileges are not automatically laid on for loved ones traveling separately, with protocol stating that 'courtesies... will not be extended' to family members of VIPs 'when the families are traveling on their own.'

But according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail, members of Infantino's family enjoyed the airport's services dozens of times while traveling without the FIFA president between 2024 and 2026.

Gianni Infantino's office reportedly requested 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their dogs

The FIFA president's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months

In a statement to The Times, Miami airport insisted these requests are dealt with 'on a case-by-case basis.' The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment but a spokesperson told The Times: 'Port courtesy requests were made to Miami international airport (MIA), on the advice of a former adviser to the Fifa president.

'Port courtesies are provided at no charge to the president of Fifa given his position as the head of an association or NGO. Mr Infantino’s family members are also entitled to request these services under MIA’s own Courtesies of Port Handbook and these are also provided free of any charge, on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of MIA.'

Infantino's position is already under threat heading into FIFA's presidential election next March, when he is hoping to be elected to a fourth term. Back in December, Infantino awarded Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize – to widespread ridicule.

During the World Cup, the Balogun affair saw Infantino accused of favoritism and caving to the White House, while the FIFA president and Trump were mocked for handing over the trophy to Spain together.

Before long, Infantino faced a mutiny over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Then earlier this week, FIFA strongly denied allegations that Infantino influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

#1826. Man United sack Michael Carrick: What happens now? Will Mauricio Pochettino take over?

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 09:39, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 20:22

Michael Carrick has been sacked as head coach of Manchester United.

A disastrous start to the 2027-28 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up only eight points from 10 matches.

Carrick had been expected to lose his job at Old Trafford off the back of the 3-0 defeat at Bournemouth on October 25, but he was instead given longer to turn the season around.

Man United have since lost to Chelsea, beaten Roma and drawn with Aston Villa.

The 20-time English champions came from two goals behind to record a 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League before twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Villa in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Man United's fans have continued to back Carrick, but the decision has now been made for the club to move in a new direction.

"Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach," read a statement from the club.

"Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

"The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."

The club's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future at the helm.

Wilcox and Berrada recommended that Carrick is removed from his position as head coach due to the team's ongoing struggles.

Carrick has taken training this week, while he arrived at Carrington on Thursday morning to be informed that he would not be remaining as head coach of the Red Devils.

Man United are not back in action until the clash with Liverpool on November 22, and the USA's Mauricio Pochettino is poised to be appointed the club's new head coach.

The United States are said to be expecting Pochettino to lead them into their two matches against Haiti on November 14 and November 18 respectively during this international period, with Man United prepared to wait for the Argentine.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup.

Man United need to pay a £7.4m compensation fee to bring him to Old Trafford at this stage, with further fees required to appoint his coaching staff, including assistant Jesus Perez.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are all available for an immediate start and have been linked with the managerial role, but Pochettino is now set for the position.

Pochettino is expected to be backed during the January transfer window, with the club planning to be active at the start of 2027.

#1824. Thomas Tuchel responds after England fans boo Ben White again

Thomas Tuchel has called on England fans to stop booing Ben White.

White was audibly booed as he replaced Trent Alexander-Arnold in the 78th minute at Wembley on Thursday evening in a repeat of what happened the last time the Arsenal defender turned out for England, during the international break in March of this year.

The animosity from England fans dates back to late 2022, when White left the World Cup squad midway through the tournament in Qatar due to personal reasons. He did not play again for the Three Lions during Gareth Southgate’s time as manager.

White ended his four-year England exile in March, when Tuchel called him up for pre-World Cup friendlies against Uruguay and Japan, but he was greeted with boos in both games.

Injury prevented White from selection for the 2026 World Cup, but Tuchel saw no issue with bringing him back into the squad ahead of this month’s Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

Earlier this week, White said supporters would not boo him if they knew the full story behind his abrupt exit from the World Cup.

But as he was introduced against Croatia, boos could be heard from portions of the England support.

“I didn’t hear the boos, to be honest. I heard the claps for Luka Modric, which is nice, because he deserves it. He’s a legend of the game, but I honestly didn’t hear the boos for Ben, and I thought we were past that,” Tuchel said in his post-match press conference.

Tuchel agreed when asked if he hoped England supporters would not boo White the next time he plays, and said he could only judge the Gunners defender on what he had seen since taking charge.

Tuchel added that he did not think the boos would force White to reconsider his decision to play for England again, insisting he had no reason to doubt the player’s commitment.

“I don’t want to think in these extreme terms at the moment. He overcame the boos the last time, I didn’t hear them this time, and he can play on a high level. He proves it week in, week out for Arsenal. That is why I don’t want to think about it at the moment.”

By Ben Knapton | 12 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 12:51

Hello and welcome to Sports Mole's live reaction blog following the sacking of Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach and Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager!

The Red Devils relieved Carrick of his duties on Thursday morning, and current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as his successor in due course.

Just a few hours later, Crystal Palace announced the dismissal of Sage as head coach, and the Frenchman is expected to be replaced by Thomas Frank.

We will bring you all the reaction and latest news coming out of Carrington and Selhurst Park below!

Carrick has been given the boot by Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox and the Glazer family after a measly one win in 10 Premier League games left the club 18th in the Premier League table.

The Red Devils' current ranking is their lowest position after 10 games of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th, and a paltry eght points from 10 matches is the clearest case against him. Furthermore, they have also gone eight league games without a win.

A 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 had already put his job at risk, yet he was given longer; that reprieve brought a defeat by Chelsea, a chaotic 3-2 Champions League win over Roma and an absorbing 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8.

United needed a 96th-minute Patrick Dorgu equaliser to rescue that point after twice trailing by two goals, but the attacking numbers were not the problem, as United out-created Villa on expected goals.

However, conceding four at home showed a defensive flaw that Carrick never solved.

Context mattered, though, as Carrick took over from the doomed Ruben Amorim in January and led United to third place and Champions League football in the second half of the 2025-26 campaign, but that credit in the bank was ultimately not enough.

Now, Pochettino is set to take over after an agreement in principle was reached this week.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss signed a new USMNT contract through 2030 after reaching the World Cup round of 16, though, so United must meet his reported £7.4m release clause.

Should Pochettino also wish to bring his backroom staff with him, Man United could end up forking out close to £10m for his services.

The Argentine's first match in charge is expected to be at Liverpool on Sunday, November 22 - nothing short of a baptism of fire upon his return to English football.

Published: 13:14 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:15 EST, 9 November 2026

Wayne Rooney has led the praise for football super-agent Paul Stretford as the industry heavyweight was honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards.

Stretford, alongside Kenneth Shepherd, received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's Awards in recognition of their longstanding careers and work on Soccer Aid for Unicef.

He has worked by Rooney's side for more than 20 years, and has recently appeared on the former footballer's reality TV show, which he fronts alongside wife Coleen.

Rooney presented Stretford with the award himself, alongside Toni Duggan and comedian Paddy McGuinness. Theo Walcott and Jamie Carragher hosted the ceremony.

Rooney said of his agent and close friend: 'Paul in particular has had a major influence on my life since I was a teenager and has guided my career.

'Both Paul and Kenneth are very deserving of this award. It is not before time and I'm delighted for both of them. The work they've done on Soccer Aid is phenomenal too.'

Wayne Rooney (centre) has lauded close friend and football super agent Paul Stretford (right)

Stretford doesn't just look after Rooney, having also worked with the likes of Harry Maguire since founding Proactive Sports Management, now known as Triple S Sports Group, in 1987.

Shepherd, meanwhile, has been instrumental in the success of the Soccer Aid initiative which has raised more than £137million for Unicef since it launched in 2006.

McGuinness added: 'I'm so proud to pay tribute to a duo who have had a profound impact on football and two figures we've both had the pleasure of working with over the years. Together, they built the Triple S Group into a dynamic force in British and international football.'

England assistant manager Anthony Barry also carried out an exclusive Q&A at the event, which saw Tyler Alexander-Arnold, brother of England defender Trent, also scoop a top award.

The brother of the Real Madrid star represents Jordan Henderson, Jarrod Bowen and Andy Robertson as well as his sibling, who saw his PLG Agency bought by Gersh talent agency in May of this year.

#1818. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed ahead of Spain showdown

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals with victory over Croatia.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley on Thursday night to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England now face a one-game shootout with Spain to decide who will win the group, and an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

As things stand, if England finish second in Group 3, their potential Nations League quarter-final opponents would be Italy, Netherlands or Portugal.

Topping the group would set up a possible quarter-final showdown with France, Greece or Denmark.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1816. Portugal vs Denmark - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 10:17, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 10:19

Portugal will officially begin life after the legendary Cristiano Ronaldo with a clash against Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday night.

Jorge Jesus' side have already booked their spot in the quarter-finals of the competition, while Denmark are battling to claim the second qualification spot in the section.

Portugal have been note-perfect in the 2026-27 Nations League, boasting a record of four wins from four matches to collect 12 points, which has left them at the top of Group A4 and already seen them secure a spot in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

Jesus' team are six points ahead of second-placed Denmark, who they beat 4-2 in the reverse match between the two sides at the start of October.

Portugal have also beaten Norway twice and Wales once in Group A4, and they will finish their league campaign away to Wales on November 17.

Selecao das Quinas won the 2024-25 Nations League, beating Spain in the final on penalties, and they are aiming to lift the trophy for the third time, having also triumphed in 2018-19.

Ronaldo has now retired from international duty, so a new era for Portugal will officially begin in this match, and it will be fascinating to see how the European nation move forward without their legendary number seven.

Denmark have a record of two wins and two defeats from their four matches in Group A4, which has left them second in the table on six points, six points behind the leaders Portugal and three ahead of both third-placed Wales and fourth-placed Norway.

Brian Riemer's side opened their tournament with a 3-2 defeat to Norway, before recording a 2-0 win over Wales ahead of their 4-2 reverse to Portugal, but a 1-0 victory over Wales last time out has left them in charge of their own destiny at this stage.

The Danes require four points from their final two matches in the group against Portugal and Norway to be sure of a spot in the final eight of the tournament, although three points may also be enough depending on the head-to-head tie-breakers.

Denmark have historically found it difficult against Portugal, only winning four of their previous 19 meetings in all competitions.

The Danes last overcame Portugal (1-0) in a Nations League quarter-final first leg in March 2025, although they went on to lose the second leg 5-2 and therefore exit the competition 5-3 on aggregate.

Portugal will be missing both Joao Cancelo and Francisco Conceicao through suspension on Saturday, while there is no Ronaldo in the squad following his recent retirement.

Nuno Mendes' absence through the injury has seemingly opened the door for Monaco's Flavio Nazinho to make a spectacular debut at left-back in this contest.

Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Joao Neves could feature as the three midfielders, while it is likely that Goncalo Ramos will be given the nod down the middle for this match.

As for Denmark, six players are one booking away from a ban, but the national side do not have any suspension issues for this match.

Patrick Dorgu is a notable absentee, having only just recovered from a hamstring injury that he suffered during the last international break.

Rasmus Hojlund has scored 16 goals in 39 appearances for his country and is once again expected to lead the line, while there could also be a start in an attacking area for Victor Froholdt.

#1814. Van Bommel labels Belgium’s Ngoy as ‘prototype of the modern defender’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mark van Bommel has labelled Belgium centre-back Nathan Ngoy as "the prototype of the modern defender" after another strong performance in the Nations League.

Belgium came from behind to defeat Turkiye 2-1 on Thursday, with Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere getting on the scoresheet following a stunning free-kick from Arda Guler.

Ngoy started at centre-back alongside Brandon Mechele, with the Lille defender winning five of his nine duels, winning possession three times and recording a team-high six clearances.

Among Belgium defenders in the 2026-27 Nations League, Ngoy leads the way in interceptions (10) and clearances (24), while he has also won the second-most duels (13).

"The central defence was very strong again. Take Ngoy. Apart from that one mistake at the start, he played a perfect game," Van Bommel said after the win over Turkiye.

"But actually, that applies to all his previous international matches. The prototype of the modern defender.

"He defends extremely cleanly, constantly anticipates, and always thinks one step ahead. He dares to defend high up the pitch and is physically very strong. He really is a top modern defender.

#1813. Manchester United: How Mauricio Pochettino will differ tactically from Michael Carrick

The Manchester United squad might want to brace themselves for what is coming their way.

Michael Carrick has been sacked and it is expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be arriving to replace him in the Old Trafford dugout.

Pochettino interviewed for the United job in 2024. He was close to getting it on more than one occasion in the years before that too.

Finally he is set to get his chance and the task is now bigger than ever, with United sitting in the relegation zone and in desperate need of a dramatic turnaround.

It is likely to start with hard work. United rank 19th for distance covered in the Premier League this season, with the team set up in a very passive manner.

Fitness has been a concern. When asked in the summer if pre-season had involved a lot of running, Youri Tielemans replied: “No. When you come back from the World Cup, you don’t do lots of running. Just chill.”

There is not going to be much chill with Pochettino around. He has a long history of getting his players working hard.

In the 2013-14 season, his Southampton side covered more distance than any Premier League team. That season, Tottenham ranked 20th.

There is not going to be much chill with Pochettino around

When Pochettino then took over at Spurs the following year, nobody ran further than them over the next four seasons.

That continued at Stamford Bridge. Pochettino’s Chelsea team ranked in the top 10% for all Premier League teams since the 2023-24 season for high turnovers.

The Blues averaged nine high turnovers a match. United are at just over six this season in that metric, and are one of only four teams in the league not to score a goal leading from a high turnover.

It might be a case of being careful what you wish for from a United perspective. After the heavy defeat to Como, Fernandes took aim at Carrick’s back-foot approach.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal target Endrick; Balogun to Man Utd

Bruno Fernandes has already revealed his dream moves after Man Utd exit

Carrick sacked LIVE: Man Utd announcement as Pochettino deal agreed

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

“It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man,” Fernandes said. “But sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people frustrated.

“I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.”

The high intensity tactical approach that United are expected to deploy under Pochettino draws into focus comments made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe in 2024.

“We’ll decide that [playing] style, plus the CEO, sporting director, probably the recruitment guys,” Ratcliffe said.

“What the style of football is, and that will be the Manchester United style of football, and the coach will have to play that style.

“We’re not going to oscillate from a [Jose] Mourinho style to a [Pep] Guardiola style. That’s not the way we’ll run the club.

“Otherwise, you’re changing everything all the time. You change your coach, you’ve got the wrong squad. We won’t do that.”

What the style of football is, and that will be the Manchester United style of football, and the coach will have to play that style

That is exactly what United have done. From Erik ten Hag they pivoted dramatically to Ruben Amorim and his insistence on a back-three system.

Carrick came in and changed that style again to a lower intensity possession approach, and now it will be all-action under Pochettino. The summer signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos do not appear to be good fits.

The Argentine will demand legs in midfield and that should be good news for Carlos Baleba, who should have a key role to play.

In defence, Pochettino will want a high defensive line to support the press but that will be a test with the resources at his disposal.

This is a team with the third-worst defensive record in the league and Pochettino must immediately address that.

Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt are much more comfortable defending their own box, meaning the mobility of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven could lead to them getting plenty of minutes.

It could be a big opportunity for Patrick Dorgu, too. Pochettino wants full-backs to hold their width, getting up and down the touchline and and allowing the wingers to cut inside.

Dorgu has the engine to do that. He has started only one league match at left-back this season but could become crucial under Pochettino, particularly if it unlocks Matheus Cunha further up the pitch.

Pochettino does not have the luxury of a pre-season. Whipping his players into shape during a campaign will not be easy. However, if he is to get the bounce in results and performances that are sorely needed, it feels essential.

By Darren Plant | 12 Nov 2026 10:22

USA head into the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final in Haiti on Saturday evening with uncertainty surrounding their head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

After Michael Carrick was sacked as Manchester United manager on Thursday, the expectation is that Pochettino will be named as his successor over the coming days.

On the back of a last-16 appearance at the World Cup, Pochettino was focused on trying to deliver a Nations League crown with USA after only making the semi-finals in the last edition.

USA have won all four friendlies since the World Cup, beating Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada respectively.

Most notably, clean sheets were kept in the 3-0 triumph over Mexico and 1-0 victory versus Canada, with 12 goals also being netted across that period.

Turkey and Belgium are the only nations to have defeated the Stars and Stripes across a nine-game stretch.

Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun should return to the starting lineup, while a decision will need to be made over whether to hand 17-year-old Cavan Sullivan a fourth cap on the right flank.

Matt Freese, Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake are all competing for the goalkeeping spot.

Miles Robinson, Yunus Musah and Ricardo Pepi are among the other experienced names who do not feature in this squad.

#1811. Man Utd confirm Pochettino as new head coach

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick's successor.

Carrick was sacked on Thursday after leading United to just one win in their first 10 Premier League games in 2026-27 (D5 L4).

Despite coming from 2-0 and 4-2 down to earn a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in what turned out to be Carrick's final game in charge, United are spending the international break in the relegation zone, sitting 18th.

It is their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th.

They have also gone eight Premier League games without a win for the second time, also doing so in April and May 2025, under Ruben Amorim.

And it is Pochettino who is tasked with turning things around at Old Trafford, despite signing a new deal with the United States following the World Cup.

He has signed a reported two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, becoming the club's eighth permanent manager since the retirement of Alex Ferguson in May 2013.

Pochettino will take charge of the USA for both legs of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti this international break, before heading to Manchester and preparing for a clash with rivals Liverpool.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 13, 2026

Pochettino has been linked with United numerous times in the past and had been in talks with the club in 2022, though they opted to appoint Erik ten Hag instead.

The 54-year-old has previous experience in the Premier League, having taken charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea across his career.

His most successful spell was with Spurs, whom he led between May 2014 and June 2019, taking charge of 202 Premier League games.

He has overseen the most Premier League games in Spurs' history and recorded the most wins (113) – that is 43 more than any other boss has managed for the club (Harry Redknapp is second with 70).

During Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, they scored 372 goals in the top-flight, which ranked fourth in the division in that time, behind Arsenal (376), Liverpool (394) and Manchester City (470), in addition to reaching the 2019 Champions League final, which they lost to Liverpool.

Of managers to oversee 30+ Premier League games, Pochettino (51%) has the 19th-best win ratio in the competition's history.

After facing Liverpool, United will travel to Sporting CP in the Champions League before Pochettino's first home game in charge of Brentford on November 28.

Bruno Fernandes is among the Manchester United players who have paid tribute to Michael Carrick following his sacking.

“Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” a statement read.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

“The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Despite overseeing just one win from the opening 10 Premier League matches of the season and leaving United in the relegation zone, the reaction from some Man United players on social media have proven just how much a popular figure Carrick was in the dressing room.

#1809. Nations League permutations: What England need against Spain to qualify for quarter-finals as group winners

England face Spain this weekend in a Nations League shootout to decide who tops Group A3.

Victory over Croatia on Thursday evening meant England officially joined Spain in qualifying for the Nations League knockout phase with a game to spare.

Though, as things stand, the reigning world and European champions lead the way with a three-point lead over England - courtesy of their victory at Wembley Stadium during the autumn international break.

Since then, La Roja have beaten Croatia and the Czech Republic twice each and just need to avoid defeat against Three Lions in the reverse fixture on Sunday to guarantee top spot and an easier quarter-final draw.

However, as England have the superior goal difference (+12 compared to +9) between the two nations, a win for Thomas Tuchel’s side in Madrid would be enough to see them top the group at Spain’s expense.

This is because the UEFA tiebreaker first looks at the head-to-head record when sides are locked on the same amount of points, and then total goal difference in the two games between the two sides.

As Spain won the reverse fixture by a one-goal margin in September, any margin of victory for England - whether it be 1-0, 2-0 or 2-1 - will guarantee top spot in Nations League Group A3.

Topping the group would set up a possible quarter-final showdown with France, Greece or Denmark, as things currently stand.

Furthermore, the group winners will be seeded for the Nations League quarter-final draw, therefore securing home advantage in their second leg ties.

Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

Were England to fail to beat Spain and finish second in Group 3, their potential Nations League quarter-final opponents would be Italy, Netherlands or Portugal.

#1806. A failed spell at Wolves almost saw him walk away from football ...now Danny Armstrong is idolised in Romania as he attempts to lead Dinamo Bucharest back to former glories

Published: 13:42 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:52 EST, 9 November 2026

The daughter says: ‘Da’. Darby Armstrong, all of two years old, is not calling out for her father, Danny.

‘She is saying “Yes” in Romanian. She can count to ten in Romanian,’ says her proud father. She may have to learn to count higher, and quickly, to chart her father’s figures in the Superliga with Dinamo Bucharest.

Armstrong sits in an upmarket restaurant in the beautiful suburbs of Bucharest with a park stretching towards a lake. He sips ginger tea with honey and engages with waiters, diners and children who approach him for a chat and a photograph.

‘Darby is a bit bemused by it,’ he says. ‘We were in the mall there and a guy wanted a pic. I could see her looking up to see what all the fuss was about.’

Armstrong could be forgiven for being ever so slightly bemused himself. At 29, he has taken a few dunts and not just from enthusiastic full-backs. Success has hardly been overnight.

‘I nearly gave up once,’ he says quietly. ‘Another time I thought it was all over and I was looking at one-to-one coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Danny Armstrong is hailed after his match-winning heroics in a crucial win over UTA Arad

He survived, though. He is a hero at Dinamo. There is a clamour on matchday when he comes out of the tunnel. The ultras, high behind a goal, chant his name with a fervour that suddenly breaks out in red flares and manic jumping.

It is a long way from Ayr. Armstrong knows he did not walk it alone. His saviours include John McGlynn, who brought him to Raith Rovers, George Cairns, who convinced him to stay at Hamilton, and Scott Sellars, the youth coach who advised him to leave Wolverhampton Wanderers for first team football.

He also took inspiration from many team-mates, including Kieran Tierney who was once his room-mate in a Scotland under-age team,

‘I was meant to be rooming with another left-back but he pulled out and this young player from Celtic came in,’ recalls Armstrong. ‘He wasn’t even in the squad initially and now he is Scotland’s best left-back alongside Robbo.

‘I used to play against KT so many times and I have great respect for him, playing so many games for Celtic, getting that move to Arsenal and coming back to Scotland to win trophies. The setbacks he has had… he’s an inspiration.

‘He has resilience. He has motivation. He took the half opportunity that was offered to him and ran with it.’

Armstrong has done the same in Bucharest. He has been bolstered by his past. ‘It builds you,’ he says of his experience. ‘There have been tough spells but you can look back and make sense of them and see how they have helped you. Football takes a lot of work.’

Armstrong has thrived in Romania since making the leftfield switch to Dinamo Bucharest

It takes a lot of belief too. That can be a capricious quality, seemingly dependent on the winds of fortune.

Armstrong can point to two hat-tricks that gave him faith in a time of need. ‘I scored a hat-trick for Hamilton in a youth game at Auchenhowie against Rangers,’ he says. ‘That came after I had been convinced to stick at it.’

He also scored three last season in the derby against Steaua. ‘That was crazy,’ he says. ‘I don’t think I have realised even yet how big it was. People tell me it was the greatest day in their lives. We hadn’t beaten them in five or six years. We were also in a bad spot with poor form. And then I score three. It gives me goosebumps even now.’

He adds: ‘There is a real football culture here. It means so much to people and I love that. It actually wasn’t too hard to come here because I had looked at it a year earlier but stayed on at Kilmarnock. When Dinamo came in and showed me videos and talked about the history, I was on board.’

There was one decisive factor. ‘I knew it was time to try to make a name for myself somewhere else. I wanted to test myself, keep myself open to other opportunities, try to get to the highest level I can get.’

He is professionally coy about the prospect of international football, having again missed out on Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest Scotland squad. He maintains the line of concentrating on his club form, having a dream to play for his country, and hoping to be noticed.

Armstrong was a big hit at Kilmarnock and has long been mooted for a Scotland call-up

His performances in Romania, though, have been so outstanding that there may be the odd glance from the Pocognoli camp at just what is happening at Dinamo. They may have to be quick as Armstrong qualifies for Ireland too.

He plays in a wide right role, with the freedom to cut inside and become a playmaker. His manager, Nuno Campos, has faith in him. He is the latest in a line of characters who have led him from doubt to conviction.

There is no hesitation. ‘It was McGlynn who saved me,’ says Armstrong. But there were previous tribulations that required the intervention of football folk and Armstrong is immensely grateful.

‘I had been going up to Hamilton from Ayr every night as a kid, playing at the weekend, and by the time I was about 15 I think I was drained. I felt I was missing out on other things in life. It was tough on my parents, too, who did everything for me. The family always sacrificed themselves for me.’

His parents told George Cairns, Hamilton coach, that their son did not want to continue. The reply was instant: ‘Get him up here and I will have a chat with him.’

The crisis passed after this talk and that hat-trick against Rangers. But further tribulations were to come.

Armstrong's relentless drive and enthusiasm have made him a standout player in Romania

Armstrong headed to Wolverhampton Wanderers, spurning an offer by Rangers under Mark Warburton and Davie Weir. ‘That was a mistake,’ he says. He was never near first team football at Wolves though the club wanted to retain him. After a chat with Scott Sellars, he took the chance to leave and start again.

‘That was very, very difficult,’ he says. ‘I did not play from May to November. I was sitting by the phone, urging it to ring with an offer. I had thoughts about packing it all in and going into coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Then an unlikely Superman came to the rescue in the shape of McGlynn, then Raith manager. ‘That changed everything, everything,’ says Armstrong.

A bounce game was organised to assess the player but Armstrong admits the team’s performance was awful. ‘I was very much part of that,’ he says.

He did much better in another friendly but budget considerations meant McGlynn could offer only a nine-game contract. ‘It was a couple of hundred quid a week but it meant everything to me.’ Five goals in nine games led to an extended contract.

‘He is a genius,’ says Armstrong. ‘He is so big on detail, detail, detail. He is a fantastic football coach. It’s an obsession for him.

‘I have never met a man like him. He saved my football career and made me believe I could make it.’

John McGlynn helped save Armstrong's career by taking him under his wing at Raith Rovers

After a spell at Ross County, Armstrong flourished under Derek McInnes at Kilmarnock and the move to Romania offered further scope for growth.

‘It was a bit difficult at first settling in but now my partner, Lauren, and Darby love it. We have made friends,’ he says.

At this a couple of waiters approach the table with grins and cheery banter. Armstrong responds with a warm handshake and that half-embrace that signals another acquiescence to yet another picture.

‘The big difference this season is the coach,’ says Armstrong. ‘He has come in and completely changed the environment and the atmosphere. He has brought fun back and he makes you want to come into training.’

Dinamo are now sitting joint-top of the league. ‘The first goal has to be European football, getting this club back to where it belongs,’ he says.

Armstrong has his sights set on an historic Romanian title and is not ruling out a longer stay

The Dinamo fans, who have not witnessed a league title in 20 years, sense Superliga glory. ‘We are a good side and we play nice stuff,’ says Armstrong. ‘But let’s take it game by game.’

He has the same laid-back attitude to his contract. ‘It expires at the end of the season and there is an option there but we leave all that to after Christmas.’

He is happy in Bucharest but knows the fate of a footballer is never predictable. ‘It is a wonderful place. The fans are great and the manager has faith in me.’

He points out that Campos wants him to be a ‘monster’. This is an instruction to be powerful and innovative in the final third.

The next night Armstrong swivels just outside the box and hits a wonderful shot to open the scoring against UTA Arad.

He then sprints towards the stand where Lauren and Darby are celebrating. He has just been a monster. But he is still a dad, in whatever language.

Terry Butcher has hailed Harry Kane as “one of the greatest” as the England captain broke the men’s all-time appearance record at Wembley on Thursday night.

On a momentous night for Kane, who lifted his Ballon d’Or trophy to the Wembley crowd before kick-off, and made sure he had the final say, notching his 92nd international goal to secure a slender England win over Croatia.

The Bayern Munich forward is now both England’s men’s all-time record goalscorer and appearance holder, and Butcher believes the country is “very lucky” to call him one of their own.

“It’s amazing,” Butcher told Standard Sport.

Butcher knows a thing or two about what it means to represent England, having captained his country seven times across terr77 international appearances.

It’s a heavy weight to bear, but a weight that you prepare to take on, and know you can lift

The defender was also an integral part of the England side under Sir Bobby Robson that reached the 1990 World Cup semi-finals, where they lost on penalties to West Germany.

Reflecting on his career, Butcher admits that while he may not have won as many caps as Kane, or previous record-holder and former team-mate Peter Shilton, it always remained an honour to represent England.
